featured_reviews.name: shikhani shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Let’s get into this new buzz in town !!
Taking a step to the really classy interiors of the SoBo.
Ground +2 level ! Take a step up to One Step Up 😍
The ground floor is designed for family time. First floor to enjoy the hip-hop music for the youngsters and 3rd level is really nice for small gatherings, social gatherings and big groups.
They usually have live screening on level 3 on all famous football & cricket matches.

Service by Mr. Bipin was top notch and no complaints on it at all.
Very well designed and curated menu of food was totally mouth watering, he guided us super well with all the dishes and the chef recommended ones.

Vegetarian, non-vegetarian and jain friendly restaurant!

Mocktail:-
Tall fruity twist :- Guys do try this it had an ultimate taste , mix of watermelon & Pineapple.
The heat killer one !

We started with :-
Pepper tomato rassam soup.
Something different ain’t it ? Like yeah taste was amazing, I dint know it would be real good ! It was served with idli crums instead of bread , so u dip it inside the rasam and 😉 enjoy it !

Quinoa gol guppa Shots it is ! Guys you all going to go ga-ga over this trust me ! You cannot miss this one here.
The shots were really well presented and mixed with tamarind and mint chutney.

Peri Peri Chicken for non veg lovers there.

Paneer Tikka Samosa with a twist instead of chutney served with Hummus ! And it was out of the blue man 😍

In salads:-
Watermelon feta cheese in salads were amazingly presented and totally mouth watering :D

Bar bites along with beer !
Rumali Tokri - huge rumali pappad sprinkled with cheddar dust and peri-peri

Coming to Mains:-
Kulcha Chole- I am in total ❤️ with their this form of Punjab ka taste 😍 with their Masala kulcha giving the taste of asli punjab

Alfredo paasta :- it was really cheesy and had a good blend of cooked paasta in the sauce.

Dessert :-
Guava Panna Cotta - Amazing texture and really worth a try ! Take my words ul love it !

Well Recommended:-

Food :- 10/10
Service :- 10/10
Service :- 10/10
Ambience:- 10/10

Loved it amazing a ❤️ experience! Do come here soon and try there remarkable menu !

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: NOSHIR KATRAK
featured_reviews.review_text:
China Garden an authentic Chinese Restaurant, situated at Kemps Corner, Mumbai.
Actually the food is authentic Chinese, but recently the ambience has changed and that is not upto the mark.
Service is not at all satisfactory. We had to literally call for the staff to keep Fork & Spoons and even spoons for the 4 different types of sauces. It is that pathetic.
They get water but glasses are not sufficient on the table.
Along with the cuisine that also serve hard drinks of your choice.
The worst to still come, the cut cucumber and cabbage was served in a plate but the cabbage was absolutely sour and smelling as well as tasting horrible. It must have been circulated from table to table and no staff over there ever bothered to taste and see whether they are offering freshly cut cabbage!
Our entire experience of China Garden has gone for a toss. A couple of years back, the service and food was really good and that's the reason we felt like visiting again. But to our dismay it was a horrible experience.
Don't know how Management can afford such type of service.
Am sure if this is the situation on one table, many other tables may experience the same.
Any ways food is good.

featured_reviews.name: Quresh “Skydiver” Cassim
featured_reviews.review_text: My family and I thoroughly enjoyed our meal at China Garden. The service was amazing and the food was delicious. The teppenyaki was exquisite. The soft chocolate mousse with vanilla ice cream is a must have. The big plate of vanilla ice cream with honey wonton noodles with extra honey was amazingly scrumptious. The manager Mr. Sharma really took care of some of the issues we had. Er go here quite often and I definitely recommend visiting this place.

featured_reviews.name: Mehernosh Khajotia
featured_reviews.review_text: I am a regular at this place and dont even have to see the menu. The food has been top class and the pricing good. Portion size is large. The Staff and owner are very friendly and Nice.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Oza
featured_reviews.review_text: I have read a lot of recent reviews where people have been complaining about the quality of food being dropped. However, I went for the first time last week and I tried vegetarian chinese there for the first time. The Ambience is is awesome. An amazing place to hangout with family and friends. Coming to food, the Corn Curd was not great though I had heard rave reviews. Manchurian is good, Honey Chili Potato is good, the steamed wontons are to die for. The sauces are simply amazing which they serve with starters. Fried wontons were a disappointment. But the major disappointment was main course. The noodles were extremely greasy with a strange smell coming out of it. The gravy with paneer was also bland. Schezwan rice is decent but I have had better than this before. The honey noodles with ice cream for dessert is the most loved dish here but it's too sweet!! Overall after all the rave reviews I have heard about this place I think I was satisfied with the the food and ambience but nothing great about it.

The most ill mannered staff has been hired at this restaurant. They need serious training about how to treat and talk to a customer.

On a hot summer day in mumbai, walked into this restaurant to take a parcel back home. My mom was like let’s have a glass of falooda while we wait. So I asked the person at the counter to add that to the order and give me with glass of falooda at the restaurant. This guy told me to go outside the restaurant and drink this glass since price of the glass of falooda was different in the parcel menu. I was like I very clearly told him that I would like to have the drink while I was at the restaurant and this disrespectful staff asked me to step out of the restaurant and drink it since hence made the mistake of punching in the parcel pricing for the falooda.

I asked him is this how you guys are trained to talk to your customers who visit you ? He said since he punched in the parcel rate for the drink I and my mother had no right to stand inside the hotel to drink it.

This was the first time I experienced such dis respectful behaviour from a restaurant manager. I’m hospitality business first thing to learn is to be kind to your clients. Or just like today you lost a customer in my and my mother ….you will keep losing out on the count… no body wants to eat at a place where respect for customer is least of their priority.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Chung Fa Chinese Restaurant is a place I’ve visited a number of times over the past few years, and it has consistently delivered a satisfying Indo-Chinese dining experience in Mumbai.

On my most recent visit, we ordered the Chicken Manchow soup, chicken crispy, and fried wantons for starters.

The soup was flavourful and well-prepared, setting a good tone for the meal. The chicken crispy also stood out as one of the better dishes that was nicely done and enjoyable. The fried wantons, however, were just about average in comparison.

Overall, both the starters and the main dishes were tasty and met expectations.

The kitchen does take a bit of time with preparation, but the quality of the food makes the wait worthwhile.

Service has generally been good, attentive and efficient without being intrusive, which adds to the overall comfort of the dining experience.

One area where the restaurant is somewhat limited is desserts. The options are minimal, and typically consist of packaged ice cream cups rather than freshly prepared items.

All things considered, Chung Fa remains a dependable choice for Indo-Chinese cuisine in the Tardeo area. It’s a place I’ve enjoyed returning to over time, and one I would recommend for a satisfying and familiar dining experience.

The menu got excellent classic dishes. The bar has a few of the best cocktails and mocktails. The food menu got good variety available. Being an old and classical restaurant, their dishes were flavorful.

Cosmopolitan (Cocktail) – a classic cocktail made with vodka, sweet n sour, cranberry juice and orange liquor, served in a martini glass. (5/5)

Orange Mix Fizz (Mocktail) - A touch of basil and lime leaves, a fizzy drink made with orange bitters. Loved the balancing of flavors. (5/5)

Chakori Kebab – Chicken chunks marinated in green herbs, especially in fenugreek, then cooked well in tandoor. Loved the margination it was flavorful. (5/5)

Peri Peri Prawns – Prawns batter fried and tossed in peri peri sauce along with a few cubes of mix peppers. Loved the crunchiness of the prawns and the sauce was coated so well. (5/5)

Mutton Rogan josh – A classical dish made in the most authentic way. Boneless mutton cubes cooked so well in thin traditional rogan josh gravy. The Doneness of the mutton was too good. I had garlic butter naan with it, which was just perfect. (5/5)

Caramel custard- The best and my favorite dessert to try in a classic restaurant like this. It was superb.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Chinese Palace is one of the older Chinese restaurants in Mumbai, reportedly around since 1972. The location, however, can be slightly tricky to find, as it is situated on the second floor of a building and set a bit inside from the main road.

We visited as a large group of over 10 people for dinner, which gave us a good opportunity to sample a range of dishes from their extensive menu.

For starters, we ordered Crispy Thai Chicken and Crackling Spinach with Chicken, along with Sweet Corn Chicken Soup. For the mains, we went with Chicken Schezwan Fried Rice, Diced Chicken Chilli, and Stewed Wantons.

The food overall was tasty, though somewhat inconsistent across dishes. The soup was good, and among the starters, both the Crispy Thai Chicken and Crackling Spinach with Chicken stood out as particularly enjoyable. However, some items like the stewed wantons and the diced chicken chilli felt a bit on the blander side, and even the Schezwan fried rice lacked the expected punch.

Portions were generous, which worked well for a group setting. They also serve kimchi as a salad accompaniment, which was a slightly unusual but interesting touch.

Service was good in terms of staff behavior, but the preparation and delivery of food did take time, especially noticeable with a larger group.

Overall, Chinese Palace offers decent food with some standout dishes, but also a fair bit of inconsistency. Worth a visit for select items, but with a bit of patience required.
